content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to recent price spikes; fails to anticipate sharp reversals or mean reversion after peaks.
- Overconfidence in short-term momentum leads to overestimation of volatility or direction.
- Model exhibits lag in adjusting to recent low prices; often fails to recognize bottoming or reversal signals.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent highs.
- Model underweights recent low prices in the 30d window, leading to delayed correction.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes, then fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled; forecasts remain too high even after price corrections.
- Model tends to ignore or underweight the influence of the most recent 5–7 days in the 30d window.
